repo.description:
### Summary

The web dashboard replaced the `$SESSION_TOKEN` placeholder in external workspace-app URLs with a newly minted API key without checking whether the app belonged to a sub-agent. Sub-agent apps are registered at runtime by code running in the workspace, so their URLs are not trusted. A sub-agent could register an external app with an allowed custom protocol (for example `vscode:`) whose URL carries the placeholder alongside an attacker-chosen destination. When the workspace owner clicked the app in the dashboard, the dashboard minted a full-access API key and opened the crafted URL with the key in it. The dashboard also did not check where any external app link sent the token: it did not verify that the link opened a known Coder IDE handler or that its `url` pointed to this deployment.

`coder open app` already refuses this substitution for sub-agent apps (GHSA-v54h-cp2w-9x4g). The dashboard did not apply the same check.

> **Note:** Exploitation requires code running as a sub-agent in the victim's workspace (for example a devcontainer or an AI agent), and the victim clicking the malicious app in the dashboard.

### Impact

An attacker who can run code inside a workspace can obtain a full-access API key for the workspace owner, and act as that user for the key's lifetime. The attacker controls the app's name and icon, so the app can impersonate a legitimate launcher.

### Patches

The dashboard no longer substitutes a session token for external apps that belong to a sub-agent, matching the CLI. For other external apps, the dashboard now only substitutes a session token when the link opens a known Coder IDE handler and points to this deployment. Other links are shown as disabled and no key is minted.

[#31208](https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/31208)

Backported to `2.38.2`, `2.37.6`, `2.36.9`, `2.34.14`, and `2.29.23`. Release line 2.35 and other end-of-life lines will not receive a patch; upgrade to a supported release.


### Workarounds

Do not click external apps listed under devcontainer or other sub-agents in the dashboard unless you trust the code running in the workspace.

### References

- Fix: #31208
- Related: GHSA-v54h-cp2w-9x4g

### Credits

We'd like to thank a customer security team and @manus-pi for reporting this issue!
repo.summary: Session token leaked to arbitrary hosts via web dashboard for sub-agent external apps
